summary: Justin McDaniel works in Buddhist and religious studies. He served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at the University of California, Riverside, and was attested between 2011 and 2026 as the Kahn Endowed Professor of the Humanities at the University of Pennsylvania.

Justin Ritzinger specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Harvard University (2003–2010) under Robert M. Gimello and Michael Puett. He held posts at Oberlin College (attested 2013) and the University of Miami (2013).
Justin Shimeld is a philosopher who completed his PhD at the University of Tasmania under the doctoral supervision of Jeff Malpas and Sonam Thakchoe.

Justin Václav Prášek (1853–1924) was an Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar and historian. He earned his Ph.D. at Charles University (~1876–1882) and studied at the universities of Munich and Berlin in 1885. He also taught Édouard Huber.

Justus Günther Grassmann (1779–1852) studied at the Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from circa 1797 to 1801. He subsequently held a position at the Marienstiftsgymnasium from 1806 until 1852.

Justus Olshausen (1800–1882) was a linguist, Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar, and Indologist. He earned his doctorate at Kiel University and studied in Berlin and Paris. He held professorships at Kiel (1823, 1830–1852) and Königsberg (1853–1858).
Justyna Wiśniewska-Singh is an Indologist and linguist. She completed her M.A. and Ph.D. at the University of Warsaw between 2001 and 2015, where she held the post of Dr in 2016.

Jvala Singh is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who completed his PhD at the University of British Columbia (2018–2024). He served as a lecturer at the University of California, Berkeley, in 2021.
Jyotirindranath Tagore (1849–1925) was active in linguistics and other fields. He received his education at the Hindu School and Presidency University (~1864–1867).

János Harmatta (1917–2004) was a Hungarian scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and Indo-European linguistics and Indology. He earned his Ph.D. at Eötvös Loránd University (1935–1940), where he later served as docent (1947) and professor (1952).

János Szerb (1951–1988) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. at Eötvös Loránd University (~1980–1982) and held posts at the University of Vienna (1982) and the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (1984–1988).

Jérôme Ducor is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied under Jacques May and earned his D. Litt. at the University of Geneva. He held posts at the University of Lausanne, Musée d'ethnographie de Genève, and the University of Geneva.

Józef Lączak (1926–1989) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Helena Willman-Grabowska at Jagiellonian University (M.A. 1952). He taught at Eötvös Loránd University, the University of Warsaw, and the University of Helsinki, later heading Jagiellonian's Indian Department (1980–1989).

Józef Reczek (1936–1988) was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Jagiellonian University (1953–1959) under Jerzy Kuryłowicz, Tadeusz Pobożniak, and Tadeusz Milewski, later becoming a docent there in 1972.

Józef Szczepan Kowalewski (1800–1878) worked in Iranian, Central Asian, and Buddhist studies, and linguistics. Educated at Vilnius University and Kazan State University, he served as professor and rector at Kazan (1833–1860) and later as professor and dean at Warsaw.
Józef Turczyński (1884–1953) held posts at the Ukrainian National Academy of Music (~1915–1919) and the Chopin University of Music (~1920–1939). He also taught Constantin Régamey.

József Budenz (1836–1892) was a linguist who studied under Theodor Benfey at Göttingen (Promotion 1858) and at Marburg. He worked as a librarian at the Hungarian Academy of Sciences before serving as professor of Altaic comparative linguistics at Eötvös Loránd University (1868–1892).
József Schmidt (1868–1933) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied under Aurel Mayr at Eötvös Loránd University (~1888–1899), where he later succeeded Mayr and served as docent from 1908 to 1920.

Jörg B. Quenzer works in Japanology and Buddhist studies. He held posts in Japanology at the University of Hamburg (attested 2016 and 2026) and served on the editorial board of Studies in Manuscript Cultures (attested 2016).

Jörg Heimbel specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Supervised by Dorji Wangchuk and Franz-Karl Ehrhard, he received his PhD from the University of Hamburg (2014) and holds posts attested in 2026 at the Göttingen Academy, University of Hamburg, and University of Munich.
